task: T4 + T5 - routes to an unconditional population, and what each would cost
constraints_binding_this_section: NO route is proposed, recommended, or characterised as best / cheapest / obvious (escalation row 9).
NO estimate of the live false-positive rate appears here, bounded or hedged (escalation row 4). Route R4 DESCRIBES a bound; it does not compute one.
The environment is offline (D14). External data is NAMED and COSTED, never fetched.

cost_basis._rule: Order-of-magnitude, from the programme's own measured throughput rather than a guess.
cost_basis.measured_daily_glob: 1,836 ticker-parquet files, 144,026 rows, full scan in 11.6 s (this pass, T3)
cost_basis.measured_targeted_tick_read: scale-space causal run: 78 events, anchor +/-1,260 s of tape each, 515 s wall total, i.e. ~6.6 s per event-window including the estimator
cost_basis.measured_minute_bar_table: event_minute_bars_v2 holds 45,925,350 rows for the 20,951-event in-scope archive

routes.what_it_needs: Daily OHLCV for every NMS common stock on XNYS/XNAS across 1,465 sessions, 2020-01-03 to 2025-10-31. Roughly 4,000-6,000 symbols x 1,465 sessions is order 10^7 rows.
routes.on_disk: NO. data/daily holds 1,836 tickers over 82 sessions (5.6% of the archive's sessions), and whether those 1,836 are a market-wide set or themselves selected is not established.
routes.what_it_would_establish: How many names cleared a >=30%-from-previous-close move on a DAILY basis, per session, across the archive span. That is a denominator for daily-resolution admission.
routes.what_it_would_NOT_establish: Anything about intraday or extended-hours firing. A daily bar cannot express a screen that polls every 20 s and admits at all hours (screen_definition.json elements 2 and 5). It answers a different question from the one the live screen asks.
routes.failure_mode: Silently substituting a daily close-to-close move for the live screen's intraday, pre/post-inclusive trigger, and reporting the result as the live rate.

cost.passes: 1 full pass over an external daily source, order 10^7 rows
cost.wall_time: minutes, by analogy with the 11.6 s measured for 1.4x10^5 rows - the scan is not the cost
cost.blocked_by_offline: YES - the data is not on disk and D14 bars fetching it

routes.route: Intraday scan replay over a historical window
routes.what_it_needs: Minute or tick data for the WHOLE market over the replay window, not the ~1,848 already-filtered tickers. Plus the reference-price rule that ambiguity A1 leaves unresolved.
routes.on_disk: NO. data/filtered holds only tickers that already passed selection; Phase 8 A10.2d confirmed the rejected-candidate population is absent from it.
routes.what_it_would_establish: The only route that reproduces the live screen AS SPECIFIED - 20 s poll, all hours, common stock on XNYS/XNAS - and therefore the only one that can produce a fire-rate rather than a proxy.
routes.what_it_would_NOT_establish: Nothing further is needed for the fire-rate question, but the result is conditional on A1 being settled first; a replay run against the wrong reference price answers a different screen.
routes.failure_mode: Running the replay on the tickers that are on disk. That reproduces the archive, not the market, and would return a fire rate near 1 by construction.

cost.passes: 1 pass over whole-market intraday data for the window; at the archive's own density this is order 10^11-10^12 rows for the full span, and materially less for a short window
cost.wall_time: the measured 6.6 s per event-window is for ONE ticker-session; a market-wide replay is 3-4 orders of magnitude more ticker-sessions
cost.storage: order 10-100 TB for the full span; a single quarter is order 1 TB
cost.blocked_by_offline: YES - the data is not on disk and D14 bars fetching it

routes.what_it_needs: Nothing new. The T-3..T+3 flanking sessions of events already in data/filtered.
routes.on_disk: YES, subject to flag_window_calendar_bug per damaged offset (CLAUDE.md universe rules) and to the 17 residual flagged sessions.
routes.what_it_would_establish: A WITHIN-TICKER contrast: how often a ticker that produced one qualifying event also cleared the screen on adjacent days. Already noted in the register as a partial patch.
routes.what_it_would_NOT_establish: The cross-ticker false-positive rate, which is the quantity risk rows 3, 4 and 9 are about. Every ticker in this route is already a selected ticker, so the population it samples is the archive's, not the market's. It bounds a different thing from the one being scoped.
routes.failure_mode: Reporting a within-ticker rate as if it were the live screen's fire rate.

cost.passes: 0 new external passes; targeted per-event folder reads over existing data/filtered
cost.wall_time: order 20,951 events x a few seconds of tape read, i.e. tens of hours single-threaded, less if restricted to a cohort

routes.route: A bound rather than a rate, from the 82-session daily window
routes.what_it_needs: Nothing new, IF and only if the 1,836 tickers in data/daily can first be established as a market-wide set for that window - which T3 explicitly did NOT establish.
routes.on_disk: PARTIALLY. The bars are there for 2024-12-02..2025-04-01; the market-wide claim is not.
routes.what_it_would_establish: For that window only - 5.6% of archive sessions, containing 2,165 in-scope events - a bound on the ratio between names clearing a daily-resolution screen and names present in the archive. A bound, on a 4-month slice, at daily resolution.
routes.what_it_would_NOT_establish: A rate, any intraday or extended-hours behaviour, or anything about the other 94.4% of the archive's sessions. And if the 1,836 are themselves a selected set, the bound is not a bound.
routes.failure_mode: Treating a 4-month, daily-resolution bound as the programme-wide false-positive rate. This is the cheapest route and therefore the one most likely to be over-read.

cost.passes: 1 pass over data/daily, measured at 11.6 s
cost.wall_time: minutes including the market-wide-set audit, which is the real work
cost.blocked_by_offline: NO for the arithmetic; YES for the market-wide-set audit, which needs a reference list of NMS common stock for the window that is not on disk

routes.NOT_COMPUTED_HERE: Escalation row 4 bars this pass from producing the bound. The route is described; the number is not produced.

sequencing_facts._rule: Facts about ordering, not a proposal. Row 9 bars proposing a route.
sequencing_facts.A1_gates_R2: Ambiguity A1 - the reference price of todaysChangePerc - must be settled before R2 can be specified, because a replay is a reproduction of a screen and the screen is not fully defined without it.
sequencing_facts.market_wide_audit_gates_R4: R4's validity depends on an audit R4 does not itself perform.
sequencing_facts.R1_and_R2_are_both_offline_blocked: Neither can start under D14 without an external acquisition, which is a procurement decision rather than a research one.
sequencing_facts.R3_is_the_only_route_that_can_start_toda: Stated as a fact about blockers, not as a recommendation. R3 also answers a different question from the one being scoped, per its own row.

questions_this_pass_could_not_answer: What todaysChangePerc is referenced to, and whether its numerator includes extended-hours trades (A1). Settling it requires an external field definition; D14 bars the fetch.

Where the >=X% momentum threshold is actually applied - the producer of the two momentum scan files is not in this checkout, so the archive's own momentum screen is still unread. Risk row 2 is only half-closed by this pass.
Whether data/daily's 1,836 tickers are a market-wide set or a selected one. T3 measured breadth; it did not establish provenance.
Which strategy defines the intended live universe for research purposes (A2).
The size of the rejected-candidate population, which Phase 8 A10.2d established is absent from data/filtered and which no route above recovers from disk.
